steps.what: Count production and record material types and measured dimensions
Copy checked production observations into the production record
Check production records and resolve quantity or dimension discrepancies

tasks.design: Capture the operator's checked counts, types and dimensions once in a native {OPS_SYSTEM} form at the machine. The form fills the production record, and the operator checks discrepancies and the exact final record before release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handwritten observations are copied into a separate production record.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reuse captured fields without changing physical counting or measurement.
tasks.still_hard: Incorrect units, mixed batches and distinguishing produced quantity from acceptable quantity.
tasks.human_edge: The operator connects recorded observations to the actual material and resolves discrepancies.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate entry; measurement and record accountability remain with the operator.

reach.task: Prepare a traceable batch observation handoff

evidence.claim: Single capture into a production-record form is plausible; the proposed operator labour saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is production observation and record maintenance, excluding operating the cutting machine and separate product inspection.

The operator produces the structured observations in s1: work order, batch, material type, produced quantity, quantity unit, measured dimensions, dimension units and observation time. Physical counting, measurement, batch selection and data capture all remain fully counted; missing or unusual fields are entered manually and checked in s3.
Existing production planning supplies work order and material identifiers before s1. No inferred dimensions, automatic acceptable-quantity flag or new planner data-entry task is assumed.
Try native forms before a custom app. The s2 saving removes only duplicate copying, not first capture; existing direct-entry or machine-fed records receive no new saving.
unknowns: Whether counts and dimensions are already captured directly
research_questions: Does capture-once remove duplicate entry after operator checks and form upkeep?

already_counted.description: Physical counts, measurement, capture and final record checking

incremental.description: Check field mappings, form changes and failed saves

approvals.approved_version: Exact production record, batch, quantities, units, dimensions and observation timestamp; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gives gross25 and net18 after7 focal upkeep;2 support hours remain visible. Range3-10% assumes recurring paper-to-system duplication, allowing mixed batches and manual corrections. Counting and measurement are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine cutting setup from job requirements

steps.what: Review work orders, blueprints, specifications and job samples
Determine cutting components, settings and adjustments from job requirements

tasks.design: Keep job review and setup choices with the operator, using current requirements in {DOCS} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. The operator reconciles specifications with the actual machine and material before choosing settings.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same dimensions can need different settings with different materials or machine condition.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional component is proposed without evidence of a repeatable, verified setup-selection subtask.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete instructions, material variation and selecting a workable setup.
tasks.human_edge: The operator connects the job requirements to the actual cutting conditions.

reach.task: Clarify missing setup requirements before release to the floor
reach.learn: Job specification ownership and escalation practice

evidence.claim: Cutting setup selection depends on material and machine context; no new labour saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is reviewing instructions and selecting setup, excluding entering controls, physical adjustment and first-article inspection.

Planning or engineering supplies existing work orders and specifications; the operator checks them in s1 and observes machine and material condition in s2. No new structured setting recommendation or unpaid engineering preparation is assumed.
Use existing native job and document access before any custom build; existing retrieval runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new component or process is introduced.
research_questions: Which setup decisions remain variable after using current validated instructions?

already_counted.description: Instruction review and contextual setup choice

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross and net0; job interpretation and setup judgement remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Sort cut material by type and size for the next destination
Stack sorted material for packaging, processing or shipping

tasks.design: Retain sorting and physical stacking with the operator using the existing handling equipment. No software-only component removes material movement.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task physically separates and moves cut material.
tasks.enabler_now: No new handling equipment or software integration is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Irregular material, mixed sizes and maintaining the required separation during handling.
tasks.human_edge: The operator notices mismatched or awkward pieces and adapts the handling approach.

reach.task: Prepare a clearly separated material handoff

evidence.claim: Physical sorting and stacking require material handling; no software labour reduction is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the operator's physical sorting and stacking, excluding later packaging and shipping.

Existing production instructions provide destination and handling requirements before s1; the operator identifies material directly. No structured type flag, new sensor feed or unpaid handler data entry is assumed.
Existing handling machinery remains baseline; its runtime is not a new saving. A hardware automation project is outside this proposal.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new component or process is introduced.
research_questions: Which handling constraints cause re-sorting or extra movement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross and net0. Existing handling equipment and downstream labour are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter cutting controls and set physical machine components

steps.what: Type cutting instructions and activate the selected computer program
Manually set cutting guides, clamps and knives to the selected setup

tasks.design: Retain deliberate control entry through the machine controls in {OTHER} and physical guide, clamp and knife setting. The operator checks the selected job and program before activation through existing procedures.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correct settings must correspond to the actual job and physical machine state.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional component is proposed for deliberate activation or physical adjustment.
tasks.still_hard: Preventing mismatched settings and recognising when actual setup differs from the instructions.
tasks.human_edge: The operator can inspect the physical configuration and reconcile it with the selected job.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in setup responsibility or activation authority.

reach.task: Provide a clear setup identity for subsequent checks

evidence.claim: Physical setup and deliberate machine-control entry remain operator work; no software saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is control entry, program activation and physical setting, excluding choosing the setup, cutting runtime and subsequent product inspection.

OTHER means native cutting machine controls. The operator's existing setup-selection task produces the chosen settings before s1; engineering provides the approved job instructions. The operator checks the actual job and control values in s1. No new structured program feed or automatic setting inference is introduced.
Use existing native controls and validated procedures; machine runtime is not human labour. Physical adjustment order follows the machine's existing procedure, with no sequence change proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new component or recurring process is added.
research_questions: Where do job-to-program mismatches occur in the existing setup process?

already_counted.description: Deliberate control entry, activation checks and physical setting

approvals.approved_version: Exact job, target machine, entered control values and selected program checked before activation; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross and net0. Deliberate activation, physical adjustment and existing runtime are unchanged.
